newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Asbrink says EMU project uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Asbrink says EMU project uncertain.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Wednesday the ruling Social Democrats were uncertain about the stability of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).

"Of course stability can in some situations be at risk. Now there is uncertainty about which countries and how many will join. Will the convergence criteria be interpreted strictly or will they be stretched to allow other countries to join?" Asbrink said.
"We don't know this today. We can only speculate about it," Asbrink told reporters at a seminar.
Sweden said on Tuesday it would not join EMU at its planned 1999 start because of low public opinion and because the project was shaky.
"We believe that EMU will take place because of strong political will in several countries. Much prestige has been invested in the project," Asbrink said.
"But of course we have seen a certain amount of worry in the past days, mainly related to the events in Germany and France, and clearly more of this can happen in the future," he added.
He said that political and economic factors made staying out of EMU the best choice for Sweden.
"When we weigh all the economic and political factors we think are important we conclude that it's best for Sweden not to join EMU," Asbrink said.
"This does not mean there are no positive sides to currency union," Asbrink said.
